title: The GST 2.0 Working Capital Test
subtitle: One year after the 22 September 2025 rate reset, a labelled composite consumer CFO must decide how to price, stock and fund working capital while RBI holds the repo at 5.25 per cent
description: HBS-style teaching case on GST 2.0 (effective 22 September 2025: 5% merit / 18% standard / 40% demerit) meeting the RBI MPC decision of 3-5 August 2026 to hold the policy repo at 5.25 per cent with a neutral stance. A labelled composite — Navtara Consumer Products and CFO Arjun Sen — must choose among passing the remaining rate cut, holding price and rebuilding margin, tightening inventory days, or refinancing working-capital lines before festive demand.
sources: GST Council, 56th meeting (3-4 September 2025). Two-rate structure: 5% merit, 18% standard, 40% demerit. Implementation 22 September 2025.
Government of India / Revenue Secretary briefing. Estimated annualised fiscal impact of rate rationalisation: about Rs 48,000 crore.
SBI Research, GST 2.0 Update (Issue 25, FY26, 4 September 2025). Weighted average GST path; CPI pass-through 65-75 bps over FY26-27.
RBI, Decisions of the Monetary Policy Committee, meeting 3-5 August 2026. Repo unchanged at 5.25%; SDF 5.00%; MSF and Bank Rate 5.50%; neutral stance.
RBI MPC minutes / Governor statement August 2026. Real GDP 2026-27 projected 6.7%; CPI 2026-27 projected 5.0%.
RBI August 2026 statement. GST e-way bills +12.4% and GST revenue +8.6% in Q1:2026-27.
PIB / GST Council materials on GST Bachat Utsav and item-level rate moves from 12% and 28% slabs.
